name: Marble physics
what: Deterministic sphere physics for marbles and balls at 60 Hz with 4 substeps: oriented boxes, cylinders, lathe shells (bowls, funnels, banked turns) and helix shells (loop-the-loops, helter-skelters), moving obstacles as pure functions of time (spinners, hammers, sliders, trapdoors, orbiting tops), speed strips, launchers, marble-on-marble bumps, plus an input-to-forces controller (grip, drag, air control, jump, slick surfaces). Same inputs give the same bits every run, in Node, Workers and the browser.
use_when: the game rolls balls or marbles over a built track or table and wants physics that feels like a toy and is deterministic enough for replays, share links, bots or multiplayer

third_party.what: three.js (npm, for src/view.js and the demo)
third_party.author: three.js authors

good_for: marble runs and marble races, rolling-ball platformers, minigolf, pinball-like tables, bowls and funnels, loop-the-loops; anything that needs replays, ghosts, share links or a server to re-run the same physics; bots that test levels headless in Node
not_for: general rigid bodies (boxes tumbling, stacking, ragdolls: use Rapier); hundreds of balls at once (marble-marble is O(n^2), fine to ~60); visible ball spin (not simulated, draw it from velocity)
how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs meticulai-marble-physics, then import from vendor/meticulai-marble-physics/src/index.js (no npm deps) and optionally src/view.js (three.js meshes for colliders); see HOW-TO-USE.md
